I'll now create the explanation and check its readability:

## What this letter says
Your mental health team met with you on 19 October 2026. They agreed to change your depression medicine (antidepressant). You were having unwanted effects (side effects) from sertraline. You will switch to a different medicine called mirtazapine. Mirtazapine can make you sleepy, especially when you start it.

## What you need to do
1. From 26 October 2026, reduce sertraline to 50 milligrams once daily.
2. On 2 November 2026, stop taking sertraline completely.
3. On 2 November 2026, start taking mirtazapine 15 milligrams once daily at night.
4. Do not drive if you feel sleepy.
5. Avoid alcohol.
6. Go to your appointment with Nurse Obi on 16 November 2026 at 14:00.

## Dates and medicines

Sertraline 100 milligrams once daily: Reduce to 50 milligrams once daily for 7 days from 26 October 2026. Stop on 2 November 2026.

Mirtazapine 15 milligrams once daily at night: Start on 2 November 2026.

Dates:
- 19 October 2026: Appointment with mental health team
- 26 October 2026: Start reducing sertraline
- 2 November 2026: Stop sertraline and start mirtazapine
- 16 November 2026: Appointment with Nurse Obi at 14:00

## Questions to ask your doctor
1. How long will the sleepiness last?
2. What should I do if I feel worse?
3. Can I drive once the sleepiness stops?
4. What side effects might I notice?

## When to get urgent help
If you feel worse, or you have thoughts of harming yourself, contact the team on 01632 960 999 (Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 17:00). At any time, you can call NHS 111 and choose the mental health option, or call Samaritans on 116 123. In an emergency, call 999.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
